title: Counting steps: best, worst and Big-O
summary: Count what an algorithm does as the input grows. Big-O is the worst case, Big-Omega the best case.

checkpoints.text: Searching for 12, which happens to be in the first cell. One check and the search is over: this is the best case.
Found after 1 check, whatever the size of the array. The best case never grows, so it is Ω(1) (Big-Omega: a lower bound).
Searching for 40, which is not there: every one of the 6 cells was checked. With n cells the worst case takes n checks, so linear search is O(n) (Big-O: an upper bound).
Two loops, one inside the other. `i` is now 1 and `j` starts again from 0: the inner loop runs all 6 times for every value of `i`.

checkpoints.at: cout << "Two nested loops over 6 items: " << countPairs(6) << " steps" << endl;
checkpoints.text: 6 × 6 = 36 steps. Doubling n to 12 would give 144: four times as many. Nested loops over the input usually mean O(n²). When the best and worst case grow the same way, we write Θ (Big-Theta): this loop is Θ(n²).
